adapter_api_usage.spring_css_signature: springCss(config?: { w: number; z: number }, samples?: number) -> { easing: string, duration: number, transition(property: string, delay?: number): { transitionProperty: string, transitionDuration: string, transitionDelay: string, transitionTimingFunction: string } }
adapter_api_usage.execution_boundary: Only the pure springCss calculation is used to prepare a finite browser animation. The Atlas adapter does not use upstream play, useSpring, MorphPath, useSequence or useReducedMotion.
adapter_api_usage.signal_timing_boundary: The upstream firm duration is 325 ms. Atlas host timing remains governed by Signal; consuming the easing does not authorize changing canonical 140/240 ms timings.

compatibility_caveats: The package core is ESM with no React runtime dependency; static vanilla use still needs the repository-approved same-origin build/module path.
The optional React entry declares React >=18 and a use-client boundary. That peer range does not establish compatibility with the actual active Hardware/Next.js owner stack.
CSS linear() and WAAPI capability must be detected by the adapter; unsupported capability leaves final state readable or uses the explicit Signal fallback.
Live reduced-motion changes, hidden-tab cleanup, rapid interruption, independent roots and unmount disposal are adapter responsibilities and require their own evidence.
The existing motion owner retains shared runtime/ticker ownership. Do not add a duplicate ticker or global animation cleanup.
Semantic state, keyboard/focus behavior, URL/history and success/permission remain owned by host controllers. Easing completion is never evidence of successful application work.

upstream_lifecycle_notes.scope: Source findings for future consumers; these APIs are not used by this adapter.
upstream_lifecycle_notes.ticker: play uses a module-scoped callback Set and one RAF, with dt clamped to 0..0.1 seconds. Its stop function only removes the callback, leaving any already queued empty frame. No hidden-tab listener is supplied. A throwing callback can interrupt scheduling bookkeeping.
upstream_lifecycle_notes.react: useReducedMotion subscribes to preference changes, but useSpring, MorphPath and useSequence only sample the preference when their target effect runs. useSpring keys its effect on Object.values(target).join(), so configuration, immediate or equal-value key changes alone do not retrigger it.
